findings.evidence: `FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:119` has `variable (A : CommAlgCat.{u} R)` and `:138` has `{B : CommAlgCat.{u} R}`; but `Trivial.lean:112` uses `{A : Type v}`, `:181` uses `{B : Type w}`, and `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.lean:175` defines `pointsFunctor` on `CommAlgCat.{w} R`.
findings.fix: Introduce separate value universes, e.g. `universe u v w`, use `variable (A : CommAlgCat.{v} R)` and `{B : CommAlgCat.{w} R}`, and keep the same proofs by delegating to `TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv`.
findings.issue: `trivialPointsMulEquiv` and its naturality lemmas restrict value algebras to `CommAlgCat.{u} R`, even though the existing points API is universe-polymorphic in the value algebra.

summary: The finite-type trivial points API is under-generalized in the value-algebra universe. The object itself may be same-universe, but its functor of points should not force `A` and `B` to live in `Type u`.
